name: Suprematism
summary: Flat geometric shapes, such as a square, a bar, a circle and a cross, that float on a white field. The picture shows no object: it shows pure feeling and the sense of space.

philosophy.core_thesis: Art should free itself from the object: pure shapes in a limitless white field give the feeling of form and of space and nothing else.
design_principles: Build the picture from 1–12 flat geometric shapes: a square, a rectangle, a circle, a cross, a bar.
Float the shapes on a white or pale field, and leave 50–70% of the picture empty.
Tilt the shapes at 10–45° from the vertical, so that they rise, fall or drift.
Limit the colour to 2–4 flat hues and black, with each shape in one flat colour.
Paint the shapes with a hard, clean edge and no brush texture in the colour.
Hold the weight in balance by size and position, not by symmetry.
Show no object, no horizon, no light source and no shadow.
anti_patterns: A recognisable object, figure or landscape

composition.layout: A few flat shapes, tilted and floating on an open white field, linked by diagonals; a large shape set off-centre and small shapes along its axis.
composition.focal_point: The largest shape, set at one third from an edge, with the strongest value contrast against the field.
composition.format: A canvas at 1:1 to 4:5; a size of 0.5 to 1m; the field is white and takes 50–70% of the area.

principles.rule: Keep 50–70% of the picture as a white or pale field, with no shape closer than 8% of the width to the edge.
Balance the large shape against 2–4 small shapes by area and distance, and hold the centre of mass within 10% of the picture centre.
Set a ratio of 4:1 or more between the largest and the smallest shape.
Align the shapes along one diagonal axis at 20–45° from the horizontal.
Make the focal shape black or red on white, with a value gap of 70% or more.
Use 3 levels: one large shape, 2–3 medium shapes and 2–5 small shapes.

palette.strategy: A white field with black and a few flat primary hues: red, blue, yellow, and sometimes a grey or a green.
palette.distribution: White field 55–70%, black 10–15%, one main hue 10–15%, other hues under 10% each.
palette.ground: A white or off-white ground, flat and unmodulated.

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Oil paint, thin and matt, brushed flat.
brushwork_and_medium.support: A fine canvas with a white ground.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: Flat, even fills with a stroke that does not show; the edge is drawn with a small brush of 3–8mm.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: 2–3 thin, opaque coats; no impasto and no glaze; a slight crackle with age is accepted.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: Hard and clean, with a small wobble of under 1mm from the hand.

light_and_modelling.light: None: the field is even and the shapes carry no light.
light_and_modelling.modelling: None; each shape is one flat colour.
light_and_modelling.shadow: None; shapes cast no shadow on the field.
light_and_modelling.temperature: Neutral white field; warm and cool shapes in contrast.

subject.typical: A black square, a red square, a cross, a floating bar, a circle, a group of tilted rectangles and a white-on-white form.
subject.figure_scale: No figure; the largest shape fills 20–40% of the picture.
subject.treatment: Pure and silent; the shapes are a feeling of form and not a thing.

surface.texture: Smooth, with a fine craquelure in old works.

works.work: Painterly Realism of a Football Player—Color Masses in the 4th Dimension
From Cubism and Futurism to Suprematism

reference_works.note: None of the three works is flagged as public domain by the museum: the ids identify them only. Look at the museum page for the image and its licence; do not copy it.

emotion.target_response: Silence and release: the viewer feels space without an object, and rest in pure form.

use_cases: poster and cover with bold geometry
brand marks and icons from flat shapes
avoid_when: The brief needs a figure, a story or a literal scene.
The picture needs warm texture or a hand-made look.

modifiers.how: Keep the diagonals; add a repeat of the shape along a path 5–10 times, bring in a ground of shards and a bright, divided colour.
Lock the shapes to a vertical and horizontal grid, add thick black lines of 10–20mm, and use only red, blue, yellow, white and black.

brush_size.note: Flat, even fills hide the stroke.
